title: The reset after a road day

sections.text: A road day is not quite finished when the engine stops. A small reset at home keeps damp cloths, loose receipts and yesterday’s lunch from becoming the first job next time. This is a routine for unpacking an ordinary day out, not vehicle maintenance or specialist equipment care.

Carry in food, drinks and the small things that need dealing with now. Put rubbish and recycling where they belong, rather than leaving a bag for the next stop. Check pockets and side compartments for wrappers, receipts and forgotten fruit.

Open the bag and separate damp cloths from maps and spare layers. Follow each item’s care instructions; wash what needs washing and let it dry fully before packing it away. A closed boot is not a drying rack.

sections.after: has an open top and is not waterproof. Treat it as a way to carry the dry bits together, not a way to protect maps or electronics from rain.

sections.text: Put back only the useful bits
Once the bag is dry, a short check is more useful than repacking everything you own. Keep the next outing simple:
Replace what you used up, rather than adding another half-empty packet beside it.
Return the map and small essentials to the same easy-to-find place.
Bring rechargeable devices inside to charge according to their instructions, then put the right cable back with them.
Leave out anything that is still damp, dirty or waiting for a repair. Deal with it before the next trip, not at the first stop.
Write down the one thing you missed

A two-line note is enough: what was awkward, and what you will do differently. Replace a missing spoon, move the map to a handier pocket or choose a different stopping place next time. Do not turn one untidy afternoon into a shopping list.

sections.after: as a starting point, then keep only what makes sense for your people, vehicle and plans. The best reset is the one that makes the next ordinary day out easier.
